cameras.name: Yashica Electro 35 GSN
cameras.note: A classic rangefinder with a fast 45mm f/1.7 Color-Yashinon lens and quiet, cinematic operation.
cameras.story: The Electro 35 GSN was Yashica's answer to people who wanted a serious camera that didn't require a film school degree. Launched in the early 1970s, it became one of the best-selling rangefinders of its era — prized for putting professional-grade optics into the hands of everyday shooters. The f/1.7 lens is remarkable — sharp in the center, gently dreamy at the edges, with a colour rendering that feels warm and analogue even on modern film stocks. Its aperture-priority metering was ahead of its time, quietly doing the math so you could focus on the moment instead of the settings. Decades later, it remains a favourite among photographers who want that unmistakable film look without fighting their gear for it.

cameras.name: Yashica Electro 35 GTN
cameras.note: The black-bodied twin of the GSN — same fast 45mm f/1.7 Color-Yashinon lens, same quiet electronic shutter, a darker, more discreet presence.
cameras.story: The Electro 35 GTN is the black-bodied counterpart to the chrome GSN — mechanically the same camera, dressed to disappear. Introduced in 1973, it carries the same Color-Yashinon DX 45mm f/1.7, the same stepless electronic shutter, and the same aperture-priority metering that made the series a classic. Where the GSN catches the light, the GTN stays in the shadows — a quieter look that suits street work and low-key shooting. This one arrived in surprisingly good condition. The original light seals had dried out but the mechanics were clean. We replaced the seals, verified the metering, and shot a test roll on a quiet afternoon. Same legendary glass. Same film look. Just a different kind of presence.
